clue.text: Sad quality in a verse received by poet's son

indicators.note: something received by another is taken inside it, so the letters for a verse go within the poet's letters

parts.note: Heinrich Heine is the German poet, his possessive giving HEINE plus an S
S is the standard abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A poem about a famous poet's son carries a melancholy tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'received by' puts A V inside HEINE'S S: the poet's name keeps its possessive S, then S for son follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaviness of heart is sorrow, so it is a quality of being sad.

clue.text: Stamp of quality in everything monarch's shown round on vessel

indicators.note: the monarch's letters are shown round, wrapping the word for everything

parts.note: HM is His or Her Majesty
everything means all
an ark is a vessel, as Noah's

explanation.surface: A royal mark appears around a ship's fittings as a sign of quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown round' signals a container, the monarch wrapping 'everything'; 'on' in a down clue puts the vessel below.
explanation.definitionFit: A hallmark is the official stamp on precious metal guaranteeing its purity.

clue.text: Risk having day off, causing rage

indicators.note: the day is taken off, so its letter is dropped from the word for risk

parts.note: risk means danger

explanation.surface: Taking a day off from a dangerous job leads to fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes D from DANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger and rage are synonyms for strong displeasure.

clue.text: Small company in pub with arrogant attitude, crowd from which bishop's excluded

indicators.note: company sits in the pub, its letters placed inside

parts.note: an inn is a pub
side is British slang for pretentiousness or swank

indicators.note: the bishop is excluded from the crowd, so his letter is struck from it
this word says some letters are taken away from the word it governs

parts.note: a rabble is a disorderly crowd
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A small firm drinking in a pub, putting on airs, with a crowd that turned away a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts CO inside INN; 'from which bishop's excluded' takes B out of RABBLE, leaving RABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconsiderable means not worth considering, hence slight or minor.

clue.text: Chief, no beginner, keeping hard grip

indicators.note: the trimmed word keeps the letter for hard inside it
no beginner tells us the first letter is lost from the word for chief

parts.note: central means chief or principal
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A chief who is no novice keeps a firm hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no beginner' drops C from CENTRAL, leaving ENTRAL; 'keeping' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral is to captivate, holding someone in one's grip.

clue.text: Shrub that is cut by artist in spring

indicators.note: the combined letters sit in the word for spring

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: that is is cut by artist, its letters split around the artist

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A shrub growing by a spring is pruned by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut by' puts RA inside IE giving IRAE; 'in' puts that inside SPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiraea is a flowering garden shrub of the rose family.

clue.text: Ruler back in power, astonishingly

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A deposed ruler astonishingly returns to power.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hidden run no indicator; 'in' is that signal, and 'back' turns RAST round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia, an absolute ruler.

clue.text: Promoted club retaining energy to keep going

parts.note: to sell is to promote an idea, so promoted gives sold

indicators.note: the club holds the energy letter inside it

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A football club that has gone up keeps its energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promoted' suggests a team going up a league; here it means sold, as in persuaded. 'retaining' puts E inside IRON.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is to persevere despite difficulty.

clue.text: Apple and biscuit nearly ready

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter of the biscuit word is missing

parts.note: a rusk is a hard dry biscuit
set means ready, as in ready, steady, go

explanation.surface: An apple and a biscuit are almost prepared as a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts K from RUSK.
explanation.definitionFit: Russet is a variety of eating apple with rough brownish skin.

clue.text: A batting hero after treatment goes on batting as well

indicators.note: goes on means the next piece is added on at the end
after treatment the letters are worked over into a new order

parts.note: a side batting in cricket is in

explanation.surface: A star batsman, after physiotherapy, carries on at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after treatment' rearranges A BATTING HERO into INTOTHEBARGA; 'goes on' adds IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Into the bargain is an idiom meaning in addition or besides.

clue.text: See honour awarded to Malta, enthralling island, making sense

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the honour holds the island letter

parts.note: Malta was awarded the George Cross, GC, in 1942

explanation.surface: Look at the honour awarded to Malta, an island that captivates, which seems reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralling' puts I inside GC. 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is reasoned thinking, the good sense of an argument.

clue.text: Strain leg moving instruments

indicators.note: moving says the letters shift into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a leg muscle while carrying musical instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges STRAIN LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Triangles are percussion instruments, metal bars bent into a three-sided shape.

clue.text: Sailor, hurt, mostly lacking vigour

parts.note: to mar is to damage or hurt

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is used, losing its final letter

parts.note: inert means sluggish, without vigour

explanation.surface: A sailor, injured, has little energy left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops T from INERT.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a seaman.

clue.text: Note following account about one poisonous plant

indicators.note: following places the note after the other pieces

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a topic
I is the Roman numeral one
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A note following a bill about someone who ate a toxic plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts TE after AC + ON + I.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, or monkshood, is a highly toxic plant.

clue.text: Material supplied by quite absorbing topic endlessly going around, along with drink

indicators.note: the word for quite absorbs the other pieces inside it

parts.note: rather means quite or fairly

indicators.note: going around means the shortened topic word is turned round
endlessly tells us the topic word loses its last letter

parts.note: an issue is a topic for discussion
ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: A fabric is supplied by someone who rambles on round a subject with a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts ISSUE to ISSU; 'going around' turns it to USSI; with ALE, 'absorbing' puts USSIALE inside RATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia leather is a durable leather tanned with birch oil, used in bookbinding.

clue.text: Content is loud — that's admitted by composer and director

indicators.note: admitted by means let inside, so the pieces go within the composer's name

parts.note: Erik Satie was a French composer
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A piece's quietness is loud, a fact the composer and conductor concede.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted by' puts IS F inside SATIE, between SAT and IE. 'that's' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To be content is to be pleased and fulfilled.

clue.text: Opportunist, unknown quantity in court

parts.note: a chancer is someone who takes risks for advantage
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An opportunist of uncertain character appears in a law court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancery is a division of the English High Court.

clue.text: Depression about central part of law altered by ruse in seat of government

indicators.note: about means the depression wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a trench is a long depression in the ground

indicators.note: central part of picks out the middle letter of law
altered says the next words are reworked into a different order

explanation.surface: A ditch is involved when the law is twisted by a trick in parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central part of' gives A from law; 'altered' rearranges BY RUSE to SURYBE; 'about' wraps TRENCH round ASURYBE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Treasury Bench is the front bench in the House of Commons, where ministers sit.

clue.text: View on women in regiment fluctuates

parts.note: to view is to see

indicators.note: women sit in the regiment, their letter placed inside

parts.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service regiment

explanation.surface: An opinion on women serving in a regiment keeps shifting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals a container; 'on' in a down clue puts the regiment piece beneath the view.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw moves up and down, so it seesaws as it wavers back and forth.

clue.text: Head of college possessing advanced apparatus supplying power

indicators.note: the college head possesses the letter for advanced, holding it inside

parts.note: a rector heads some colleges

explanation.surface: A college principal owns some cutting-edge power equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of' suggests taking a first letter; here 'Head of college' is the rector. 'possessing' puts A inside RECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor generates energy for power stations.

clue.text: Behave playfully and throw publication up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to lob is to throw high
a mag is a magazine

explanation.surface: Someone acts playfully and tosses a magazine upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LOBMAG backwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To gambol is to skip and frolic like a lamb.

clue.text: Calm promise to get silver for queen

indicators.note: the promise word is to get one letter in place of another
for marks the swap: the silver letters stand in place of the queen's letter

parts.note: to assure is to promise
R is regina, queen
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A soothing pledge sees a monarch rewarded with silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get silver for queen' replaces R in ASSURE with AG.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage is to soothe or ease pain or fears.

clue.text: Soldier after revolution in island put on trial

indicators.note: the turned soldier sits in the island

parts.note: Arran is an island off the west coast of Scotland

indicators.note: after revolution means the soldier letters are turned round

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier after an uprising on an island is brought to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revolution' turns the soldier round; 'in' puts him inside ARRAN, an island off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to call someone before a court to answer a charge.

clue.text: Silly to use some china needlessly

indicators.note: use some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: It is foolish to use the good china when it is not needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means pointless and foolish.

clue.text: Fish interested initially by insect that's glittering

parts.note: brill is a flatfish

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of interested

parts.note: an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A fish shows early interest in a sparkling insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'that's' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant means shining brightly, sparkling.

clue.text: Open communal meal

definitions.meaning: ... describes a mouth wide open in wonder
the love feast of the early Christians

explanation.definitionFit: Gaping wide open; also the Greek word for love, naming an early Christian fellowship supper.

clue.text: Game getting noisy, disc being moved to the end

indicators.note: the disc letter is being moved from its place to the end of the word

parts.note: loud means noisy
O is disc-shaped

explanation.surface: A game turns rowdy when a counter is shifted to the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disc being moved to the end' shifts the O of LOUD to the end. Discs also fit the board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a board game played with dice and counters.

clue.text: One backing theatrical venture put in small effort, surprisingly

indicators.note: the backer is put in the other pieces, placed inside them

parts.note: a try is an attempt or effort
an angel is a financial backer of a stage show

explanation.surface: A theatre investor made little effort, oddly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places ANGEL inside S + TRY, between TR and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangely means in an odd or unexpected way.
